title: Trdelnik
subtitle: Czech cinnamon chimney cake
excerpt: A soft dough is rolled into a rope, wound in a spiral around a spit or rolling pin, coated in cinnamon sugar, and baked until golden. Trdelnik is the sweet pastry of Czech and Slovak Christmas markets. This oven version captures the flavour without the need for an open fire.
sourceNotes: Trdelnik is a sweet pastry baked around a wooden spit. It is popular at Czech and Slovak Christmas markets. The dough is rolled, wrapped in a spiral, and coated in cinnamon sugar. The origins are disputed -- Slovakia also claims the dish.

content.text: Trdelnik is easiest to make using a greased rolling pin as your spit. The dough winds around it in a tight spiral and bakes upright in the oven. Slide the cooked cake off while still warm -- once cool it grips too firmly.

items.prepNote: plus 100g mixed with cinnamon for coating

content.text: Mix flour, baking powder, salt, and 50g caster sugar in a bowl. Add eggs, warm milk, melted butter, and vanilla. Mix to a smooth dough. Cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Mix 100g caster sugar with 2 tsp cinnamon in a shallow tray.
Divide dough into 6 pieces. Roll each piece into a long rope about 60cm. Grease a rolling pin generously.
Wind the dough rope in a tight spiral around the pin, overlapping slightly. Press well to seal. Brush all over with melted butter and roll in the cinnamon sugar to coat.
Stand the rolling pin upright or balance across the sides of a roasting tin. Bake at 180°C for 18-20 minutes until golden. Slide off carefully while warm.

items.cause: Not pressed firmly enough when winding
items.fix: Overlap each layer slightly and press well when winding. Dampening the overlapping edges with a little water helps them stick.

content.text: Czech and Slovak Christmas markets. Sold hot from rotating spits over charcoal. Now popular as street food across Central Europe, especially on Prague's Old Town Square.
